# Use Case: View Veterinarians

## Overview

**Use Case ID:** UC-002   
**Use Case Name:** View Veterinarians   
**Primary Actor:** Visitor   
**Goal:** Browse the list of veterinarians employed at the clinic along with their specialties.   
**Status:** Approved   
**Requirements:** [FR-003, NFR-001, NFR-002, NFR-003, C-010, C-011](../requirements.md)

## Preconditions

- At least one veterinarian is recorded in the system (see A1 otherwise).

## Main Success Scenario

1. Visitor clicks the "Veterinarians" link in the navigation bar.
2. System retrieves the first set of veterinarians.
3. System renders the veterinarians grid showing, for each vet, the first name, last name, and a comma-separated list of
   specialties (or "none" if no specialties are held).
4. As the Visitor scrolls toward the end of the grid, the system fetches and appends the next chunk of veterinarians
   until all entries have been loaded.

## Alternative Flows

### A1: No Veterinarians Registered

**Trigger:** The clinic has no veterinarians recorded (step 2).
**Flow:**

1. System renders the veterinarians grid with no rows.
2. Use case ends.

## Postconditions

### Success Postconditions

- The veterinarians grid is rendered with all loaded entries.
- No data is modified.

### Failure Postconditions

- On data-access errors, the application error view is shown and no vet list is displayed.

## Business Rules

### BR-001: Lazy Loading

Realizes [GR-002: Lazy Loading of Lists](../business_rules.md#gr-002-lazy-loading-of-lists).

The list in question is the veterinarians grid.

### BR-002: Specialty Ordering

Realizes [GR-003: Deterministic Ordering](../business_rules.md#gr-003-deterministic-ordering).

The order in question is a vet's specialties, alphabetically by name.

### BR-003: Anonymous Access

Realizes [GR-001: Anonymous Access](../business_rules.md#gr-001-anonymous-access).
----
# Development View

**Question:** How is the code organized, built, and kept honest?  
**Artifacts:** this document, [`testing.md`](testing.md) (the testing half of this
view), `CLAUDE.md` (the short form an agent always has loaded)  
**Notation:** Markdown  
**For the agent:** the most important view, and the one to read **before writing
anything** in `src/main/java/`. Every rule here saves a correction in every use
case.

Most of what follows is **enforced executably** by
`src/test/java/ai/unifiedprocess/petclinic/ArchitectureTest.java` (ArchUnit, runs
with `./mvnw test`). Each rule names the section it comes from, so a failure
points straight back here. If you change a convention below, change the matching
rule in the same commit — a rule that contradicts this document is the rule

These rules are the harness for use cases that have **not been written yet**, so

## Test class naming — `UC<NNN><UseCaseName>Test`

Tests that verify a use case are named after the use case, **not** the view. Format:
`UC<NNN><UseCaseNameInPascalCase>Test`, e.g `UC001ViewWelcomePageTest`, `UC004FindOwnersByLastNameTest`,
`UC007AddPetToOwnerTest`. The `NNN` matches the `UC-NNN-*.md` file in `docs/use_cases/`.

If a view is touched by multiple use cases, write one `UC<NNN>…Test` class per use case rather than one `XxxViewTest`
covering all of them. Keep the test file in the **same package as the view under test** and name the class after the UC.

**Exception — cross-cutting tests.** `ArchitectureTest` (the ArchUnit rules behind
[`development.md`](development.md)) and `PetclinicApplicationTests` verify no single use case, so they sit in the
root package under their own names. Everything that *does* verify a use case follows the format above.

## `@UseCase` on every test method

Every `@Test` method that verifies UC behaviour must carry `ai.unifiedprocess.petclinic.UseCase` **on the method**
(never on the class — the annotation is `@Target(METHOD)` and cannot go on a class):

```java
@Test
@UseCase(id = "UC-004", scenario = "A2: Exactly One Match", businessRules = "BR-001")
void exactlyOneMatchNavigatesDirectlyToOwnerDetails() { ... }
```

- `id` — required, matches a `docs/use_cases/UC-NNN-*.md` file.
- `scenario` — optional, defaults to `"Main Success Scenario"`. Set it for alternative flows (`"A1: Validation Errors"`,
  `"A2: Owner not found"`).
- `businessRules` — optional array of BR IDs. One rule as `businessRules = "BR-001"`, several as
  `businessRules = {"BR-001", "BR-002"}` — **never** as one comma-separated string `"BR-001, BR-002"`.
  `UseCaseTraceabilityTest` rejects anything that is not a bare `BR-NNN` identifier.

- **Placement** — `@UseCase` belongs on a method of a `UC<NNN><Name>Test` or, for a use case that needs a browser, a
  `UC<NNN><Name>IT`, and nowhere else; the `NNN` in the class name must match the `id` it annotates. A journey test does not borrow it to claim one of the use cases it walks through;
  that is what `@TestCase` is for. `UseCaseTraceabilityTest` enforces both halves.

This is the machine-readable spec → test link. `docs/` is the source of truth, so every test points at the exact spec
element it covers.

## `@TestCase` on every journey test

Every `TC<NNN><Name>IT` class must carry `ai.unifiedprocess.petclinic.TestCase` **on the class** (never on a method —
the annotation is `@Target(TYPE)`), because a test case has exactly one coverage unit: the journey.

```java
@TestCase(id = "TC-003", useCases = {"UC-003", "UC-004", "UC-007", "UC-009"})
@SpringBootTest(webEnvironment = WebEnvironment.RANDOM_PORT)
@Import(TestcontainersConfiguration.class)
class TC003VisitBookedForNewCustomerIT extends AbstractBasePlaywrightIT { ... }
```

- `id` — required, matches a `docs/test_cases/TC-NNN-*.md` file, and must agree with the `NNN` in the class name.
- `useCases` — required, the journey's itinerary: exactly the use cases the document's Flow table links, no more and no
  fewer. This is the part the class name cannot express, and it is what the annotation is for — add a step to the Flow
  without adding it here and `TestCaseTraceabilityTest` says so.

The two annotations split cleanly: `@UseCase` on a method of a `UC<NNN>…Test`, `@TestCase` on a `TC<NNN>…IT` class.
Each sensor rejects its own annotation anywhere else.

# ADR-004: Package by feature with `ui` + `domain`, and no service layer

**Status:** Accepted   
**Date:** 2026-09-17   
**Affects:** Logical View, Development View

## Context

An AI coding agent implements one use case at a time. Without an explicit rule
for where code goes, each use case arrives with a slightly different structure —
a service here, a mapper there, a DTO because the last prompt mentioned one. The
result is not wrong in any single place and unmaintainable as a whole.

A layered `controller/service/repository/dto` structure would give an agent four
plausible homes for every piece of logic and a reason to create a class in each.

## Decision

**Package by feature.** One package per feature (`owner`, `pet`, `visit`, `vet`,
`welcome`, plus `core` for the shell), and inside each exactly two sub-packages:

- **`ui`** — Vaadin views, forms, route parameter holders,
- **`domain`** — records and the `<Entity>Repository` holding the jOOQ queries.

**No service layer, no DTOs, no mappers** until a use case demonstrably needs
one. Query logic stays next to its use until duplication justifies extraction.
Cross-feature access goes through the other feature's `domain` package; the only
exception is naming a view class as a route token.

`ArchitectureTest.featuresHaveOnlyUiAndDomain`, `noServiceOrDtoLayer`,
`domainDoesNotDependOnUi`, `domainIsFreeOfVaadin` and `noCyclesBetweenFeatures`
enforce this.

## Consequences

- **"Where does this go?" has one answer,** and a wrong answer fails the build
  rather than the review.

UC-002 is implemented and `./mvnw test` is green: 66 tests, 0 failures, including the 19 ArchUnit rules and all four traceability sensors. I haven't committed anything.

**What I added**

- `vet/domain/Vet.java`: a record of id, first name, last name, and the vet's specialty names (`Serializable`).
- `vet/domain/VetRepository.java`: `findPage(offset, limit)` and `count()`. It loads each vet's specialties in the same query with `multiset`, ordered by name (BR-002), and is `@Transactional(readOnly = true)`.
- `vet/ui/VetsView.java`: a `@Route("vets")` view inside `MainLayout`, matching the existing "Veterinarians" nav link. It is a `Grid` with First Name, Last Name, and Specialties columns, fed by a callback data provider so rows load in chunks as the user scrolls (GR-002). A vet with no specialties shows "none".
- `src/test/.../vet/ui/UC002ViewVeterinariansTest.java`: six browserless tests covering the main flow, specialty order, "none", chunked fetching, anonymous access, and the empty-clinic alternative flow (A1). Each carries `@UseCase`.

**Choices you may want to change**

- **Vet order:** the spec's ordering rule (GR-003) doesn't cover the vet list itself, so I ordered by id. Paging needs a stable order, and this is the simplest one.
- **Column headers:** "First Name", "Last Name", "Specialties". The spec gives no header text.

**What is not verified**

- **Scroll-triggered loading:** the browserless test checks that a page request returns only the requested rows. It can't scroll, so the "fetch more as you scroll" behaviour needs a Playwright `*IT` test, which I didn't write.
- **`./mvnw verify`:** not run. It needs the Playwright browser setup and the frontend build.
- **Status line:** `UC-002` is still `Approved`. The `coverage-check` skill that the project requires before changing it isn't among the skills I can invoke here. Once that audit has run, the status can go to `Done`.

**Environment:** Docker isn't available, so I used the project's local Postgres path (`vb-postgres`, which the pom and test config already expect). That is how `generate-sources` produced the jOOQ classes and how the tests ran against a real database.
